_doc: L3 calibration set (Hamel level 3): hand-labeled trajectories used to CALIBRATE the deterministic rubric judge — NOT a raw Likert opinion. Each item is a candidate answer to a scenario, hand-labeled pass/fail against that scenario's 'Eval check' rubric. eval/l3-judge.mjs scores each candidate with the SAME rubric-keyword judge it would apply to a live trajectory, then reports agreement (accuracy / F1 / Cohen's kappa) vs these gold labels. The gate is kappa>=0.6 (Hamel: a judge you can trust). 12 trajectories (>=10 required), balanced pass/fail.

trajectories.candidate: Switch the presigned PUT to a presigned POST policy with content-length-range, and re-validate size server-side via HEAD after upload. PUT cannot enforce Content-Length on S3.
trajectories.label: pass

trajectories.candidate: Just set a larger Content-Length header on the presigned PUT and S3 will enforce the limit; PUT enforces size fine.
trajectories.label: fail

antiKeywords: validate only on upload is enough
trajectories.candidate: Validate by magic bytes on the write side AND on the read side force a safe Content-Type plus Content-Disposition: attachment and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. The bug is two-sided.
trajectories.label: pass

antiKeywords: validate only on upload is enough
trajectories.candidate: Add a Content-Type allowlist check on upload. That's enough; validate only on upload is enough to stop the stored XSS.
trajectories.label: fail

antiKeywords: allow svg it is an image
trajectories.candidate: Refuse SVG from untrusted users; if you must accept it, rasterize to PNG in a sandbox and discard the original. SVG is an XML document, not an image.
trajectories.label: pass

antiKeywords: allow svg it is an image
trajectories.candidate: Allow SVG, it is an image format; just strip a couple of script tags and serve it normally.
trajectories.label: fail

trajectories.candidate: The invisible cost is orphaned multipart uploads. Find them with rclone backend list-multipart-uploads and prevent recurrence by setting a lifecycle rule to abort incomplete multipart uploads after N days.
trajectories.label: pass

trajectories.candidate: Your bucket listing is just slow; run ListObjects again and the numbers will reconcile. Nothing is hidden.
trajectories.label: fail

trajectories.candidate: Use rclone (or R2 Super Slurper), budget the one-time exit egress at $0.09/GB, and rebuild the control plane (events, lifecycle tiering) on the target — S3-compatible ports the data plane only.
trajectories.label: pass

trajectories.candidate: It's S3-compatible, so just swap the endpoint URL and you're migrated. No extra cost, nothing else to do.
trajectories.label: fail

trajectories.candidate: ACLs are disabled by default now (BucketOwnerEnforced) and Block Public Access is on. Stop using object ACLs — use a bucket policy or, better, a CDN in front. Audit whether someone disabled BPA.
trajectories.label: pass

trajectories.candidate: R2 cannot do certified WORM (Bucket Locks are governance-grade). Route to S3 or B2 compliance-mode Object Lock, and enable Object Lock at bucket creation — it can't be retrofitted.
trajectories.label: pass
